takeaway: Type I fibres are red, slow, oxidative, with low myosin ATPase; type IIb are white, fast, glycolytic, with high myosin ATPase.

question.text: Regarding skeletal muscle fibres, which of the following statements is true?

answer.text: Type I fibres have a low myosin ATPase content.

lines.text: Type I fibres are the red, slow ones, packed with myoglobin and a rich capillary supply.
That gives them a high oxidative capacity, so they are built for endurance, like the postural soleus.
They reach peak tension in 80–200 ms, so they are slow.
lines.say: They reach peak tension in eighty to two hundred milliseconds, so they are slow.

lines.text: And their myosin ATPase content is low: look, this battery is nearly empty.
lines.say: (sigh) And their myosin ATPase content is low: look, this battery is nearly empty.

lines.text: Type IIb fibres are the white sprinters, with a big glycogen store and lots of glycolytic enzymes.
They run on anaerobic respiration, so few mitochondria, and a high myosin ATPase.
So the true statement: type I fibres have a low myosin ATPase content.
lines.say: So the true statement: type one fibres have a low myosin ATPase content.
